target_customer: Operators of campus-like private sites: universities, resorts, airports and retirement communities
problem: Operators of private campuses need cheap, driverless local transport, and a driver is the main cost of a conventional shuttle.
business_model: Monthly rental or subscription of self-driving shuttles (golf-cart style vehicles) to site operators

founders.name: Nalin Gupta
education: Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute or IIT Kharagpur Robotics Research Group (METRO 2016 says the three founders are graduates of these; not attributed per person)
founders.background_notes: Later a repeat YC founder per his YC profile.

founders.name: Srinivas Reddy Aellala
education: Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute or IIT Kharagpur Robotics Research Group (not attributed per person)
founders.background_notes: YC profile lists later roles at Serve Robotics and Nvidia, which are after Auro.

founders.name: Jit Ray Chowdhury
education: Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute or IIT Kharagpur Robotics Research Group (not attributed per person)

exit.reason: All-stock deal; the Auro team became Ridecell's autonomous driving division

competitors.name: Google self-driving car project
competitors.what: Self-driving cars tested on public roads

technical_complexity.rationale: Full autonomy stack (lidar, radar, cameras, GPS) retrofitted on golf carts and a planned vehicle with no steering wheel. Restricting to private campuses reduced difficulty, but safety validation remained hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Autonomy software took years of founder robotics work (since 2011 per Ridecell), but the approach of low-speed geofenced shuttles was open to well-funded rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied the campus wedge in sources found. Ridecell, a carsharing platform, bought Auro in October 2017.

market_need_then: MIT Technology Review (2015-08) reported test deals at a university, retirement community and resort and argued private campuses offered an easier path than public roads. Pilot at Santa Clara University began in 2015.

branding.domain_note: Used auro.ai and aurobots.com (auro.ai loads a frame from aurobots.com)

identity.visual_style: Golf carts retrofitted with sensors, campus branded; a Santa Clara student paper reported a proposal to paint it in school colors and call it Bronco Mobile, unconfirmed

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by TechCrunch, MIT Technology Review and Quartz as a campus pilot, but no evidence of brand assets, community or recognition beyond robotics press.

outcome_analysis: Auro built self-driving shuttles for private campuses, ran a Santa Clara University pilot from 2015, raised a $2M seed led by Motus Ventures in May 2016 and was acquired by Ridecell in an all-stock deal in October 2017 where the team became Ridecell's autonomous division. Price and investor returns were not disclosed, so whether this was a strong exit or a soft landing is not public.
notes: Founding year sources conflict (2013 per Ridecell release, 2015 elsewhere); 2013 used. Founder education is only given collectively by METRO. Companies like EasyMile, Navya and Local Motors appeared in search results but none with a source dated near August 2015, so they are not listed. Search results reported 2016-05 seed date from the article date. auro.ai site is a frameset pointing to aurobots.com, not read further.
